text: The repressilator is built from three repressor genes connected in a ring, with each gene repressing the next one in the cycle.
explanation: This is true: the repressilator (Elowitz & Leibler, 2000) consists of three transcriptional repressors arranged in a cyclic ring topology, where each represses the next gene in the sequence, creating a delayed negative feedback loop capable of sustained oscillation. This ring architecture -- rather than a single autoregulatory gene or a two-gene mutual-repression switch -- is what distinguishes an oscillator from a bistable toggle switch.
